PullRequest.Title: chat: allow cloud sandbox creation from the editor window
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Today the editor window can only **discover and resume** existing cloud sandbox sessions; creating a new one requires the Agents window. This PR lets users create a cloud sandbox session directly from the editor's chat session picker, with the same draft experience the Agents window offers (repository, model, mode, approvals).

## Design

A sandbox environment does not exist until it is provisioned, so a new session cannot be drafted under an environment's session type. Instead:

1. The editor registers a single **"Cloud"** creation type (`SessionType.CloudSandbox`). New chats are drafted under it.
2. On first send, `newChatSessionItem` provisions the sandbox (Mission Control task → connect), confirms the draft's picks with the host, and returns an item under the **environment's** session type; the chat infrastructure rebinds the untitled draft to it.
3. Because the draft has no backend, everything the chat input normally reads from a live Agent Host connection is supplied for the draft itself — mirroring the Agents window's own draft layer.

While the sandbox type is registered it replaces the extension's cloud agent in the editor picker, so there is always exactly one "Cloud" entry whose backend follows `chat.agentHost.cloudSandbox.enabled` (as in the Agents window).

## What changed

**Shared (`workbench/contrib/chat/browser/remoteAgentHost`)**
- `CloudSandboxSessionContribution` — lifts `_provisionSandbox()` / `trackSessionCreationProgress()` out of the Agents-window subclass so both windows share one provision → seed → connect path; populates the connection customization with `resolveInitialSessionConfig` and `modelIdentifierAliases`.
- `cloudSandboxSessionConfig.ts` — moved here from `vs/sessions` so both windows share the draft vocabulary; adds `resolveCloudSandboxSessionConfig` (host confirmation), `createCloudSandboxDraftOptionGroups`, `readCloudSandboxDraftConfig`.
- `CloudSandboxSessionListController` — tracks provisional repositories and draft config per session; resolves the working directory to the chosen repository, or explicitly leaves it to the host (`null`) for an empty sandbox.
- `EditorCloudSandboxSessionContribution` — the creation type, its option groups (repository / mode / approvals), a `CloudSandboxModels` pool fed by the cloud catalog, "Search Repositories…" (delegates to the extension's picker), and `newChatSessionItem` with a cancellable progress notification.

**Chat infrastructure**
- `AgentHostSessionHandler` — new config hooks `resolveInitialSessionConfig` and `modelIdentifierAliases`; `RequestedWorkingDirectory` lets a type say "host chooses" without local fallbacks.
- `chatServiceImpl` — re-keys the carried intended model when a draft materializes under a different session type.
- `constants.ts` — `isVisibleEditorChatSessionType` hides `copilot-cloud-agent` while `cloud-sandbox` is registered.
- `chatViewPane` — when an empty draft's session type is withdrawn (feature turned off), starts a fresh default draft instead of leaving the picker on a dead type.

**Agents window**
- Host group, creation provider, and workspace icon now use "Cloud" / `$(cloud)` to match; `CloudSandboxSessionsProvider` reuses the shared config validation. No behavior change otherwise.

### Repository picker rules (same as the cloud agent's)
- Single tracked repository (origin first, else first GitHub remote) → no picker.
- Multi-root → one entry per root, in workspace order.
- Empty window / no GitHub remote → "Select Repository" placeholder + "Search Repositories…"; leaving the placeholder starts an empty sandbox.

## How to test

1. Sign in with an account that has cloud sandbox access; enable `chat.agentHost.cloudSandbox.enabled` and `chat.remoteAgentHostsEnabled`.
2. Editor window, chat session picker → **Cloud**. Check the pickers: model (from the cloud catalog), Agent Mode, Approvals, and Repository per the rules above.
3. Send a first message: progress shows "Setting up cloud container" / "Connecting to cloud container"; the draft becomes a live sandbox session running the picked model/mode/approvals.
4. Disable the sandbox setting with an empty Cloud draft open: the picker flips to the extension's Cloud entry.
5. Verify the Agents window still creates sandboxes as before.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run eslint -- <changed files>`, `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed
- Browser unit runner (`node test/unit/browser/index.js --browser chromium --run …`):
  - `editorCloudSandboxContribution.test.ts` — 88 passing
  - `cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.test.ts` + `constants.test.ts` — 146 passing
  - `chatService.test.ts` (`rekeyIntendedModel`, `backfillTransferredModel`) — 8 passing
  - `agentHostFilterService.test.ts` — 30 passing
- The Electron unit runner (`scripts/test.sh`) was not usable in my container due to a pre-existing module-fetch flake that reproduces on `main`; the browser runner was used instead. `copilotChatSessionsProvider.test.ts` could not be loaded by either runner here (import updated for the moved module; typecheck covers it).
- Not covered by unit tests: the chat view pane's draft recovery on feature disable, and end-to-end model/config carry against a live sandbox — please exercise steps 2–4 manually.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed observer, full observable dependency chain, after-restored registration, IPC implementation, and global serialization are all directly traced. Exact duration varies with the number and type of workspace roots and Git extension readiness, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Extension-host IPC calls plus Git repository discovery/initialization filesystem and subprocess work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On a cold window the work grows once per unresolved workspace root; although the observable mapper starts promises together, `_openRepositorySequencer` makes effective concurrency one, so elapsed Git work grows approximately with the sum of per-root open/initialization times.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Eager background I/O and serialized Git/extension-host contention that reduces startup and Git responsiveness
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff, repository resolution was consumed through `_workspaceRepositories` by `CloudSandboxSessionListController`; with no discovered sandbox environment/provider, enabling the feature did not itself observe that graph or open every workspace root just to build creation options.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: After restoration, merely enabling cloud sandboxes creates an always-observed draft-option graph, immediately resolving all workspace roots so repository picker choices are ready before the picker or a Cloud draft is requested.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added constructor autorun reads `_draftOptionGroups` at line 229 whenever the contribution is enabled, even without a Cloud draft. That transitively reads `_workspaceRepositoryChoices` and the cached `repositories` array, whose mapper calls `_resolveRepository(root)` for every workspace root.
Findings.Title: Defer workspace-wide Git opening until Cloud is used
Findings.Impact: Opening any editor window with cloud sandboxes enabled can start serialized extension-host/Git repository initialization for every unresolved workspace root, consuming filesystem/subprocess/IPC capacity and delaying other Git and startup work in large multi-root workspaces even when the user never opens Chat or selects Cloud.
Findings.Evidence: `_draftOptionGroups` reads `_repositoryOptionGroups`, which reads `_workspaceRepositoryChoices`; its `repositories` mapper invokes `_resolveRepository`, and unresolved roots call `IGitService.openRepository`. `GitService.openRepository` waits up to 10 seconds for the Git delegate, while `MainThreadGitExtensionService.openRepository` performs extension-host `$openRepository` IPC, queues all opens through one `Sequencer`, and waits for each repository's `HEAD` before advancing. Thus a workspace with N roots not already known to `IGitService.repositories` causes N cold repository-open operations serially, independent of Cloud UI use.
Findings.Recommendation: Do not keep `_draftOptionGroups` observed solely to precompute picker state. Start observing/resolving repositories when `getNewChatSessionInputState` or the Cloud draft content provider is first used (and retain the observation while a draft is active), while continuing to use already-open repositories for discovery filtering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or restore an editor window with cloud sandboxes enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The contribution is instantiated at WorkbenchPhase.AfterRestored. Cloud discovery remains asynchronous, but the new draft-option autorun immediately observes repository choices and starts Git repository opening off the direct restoration await path; this work still competes with startup and extension-host/Git activity.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open and initialize a Git repository through extension-host `$openRepository`, then wait for repository `HEAD`
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold call for each workspace root not already present in `IGitService.repositories`; cached by root while the observable remains observed
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Repository resolution was observed by environment-backed list controllers; an enabled window with no discovered sandbox provider did not open every root merely to prepare creation options.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not directly awaited by workbench restoration, but serialized extension-host/Git work competes with startup and other Git operations

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Get account identity and list cloud sandbox sessions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced discovery at a time; retries are stale/focus/account driven and incremental where applicable
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same editor discovery path already ran before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous discovery populates history and is not on editor restoration's direct await path

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of workspace roots not yet registered with the Git service; effective Git-open cardinality is one per unresolved root.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable mapping creates promises for roots, but `MainThreadGitExtensionService._openRepositorySequencer` serializes repository opens globally, so effective concurrency is one. Sandbox discovery separately coalesces overlapping scans.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: `mapObservableArrayCached` caches each root while observed, so successful and negative resolutions are not repeated until roots/observation change. Git repositories already registered avoid IPC. Discovery has in-flight coalescing and stale intervals.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new always-live observable read, root mapper, Git delegate IPC, and sequencer are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of multi-root workspaces and per-root Git initialization cost vary, but the eager calls and serialization are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager-work regression: creation-picker preparation now opens all unresolved repositories without first use of Cloud.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a new Cloud draft and choose repository/model/config options
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Draft content and option groups are local. Model catalog loading starts on draft/input-state access; repository search runs only when explicitly selected by the user.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the account-scoped cloud model catalog
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared in-flight request per account/generation; repeated draft/content calls coalesce, explicit retry or account change can issue another
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The editor had no sandbox creation draft model pool; the shared catalog machinery already served sandbox models elsewhere.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Populates model choices; request is started lazily when the Cloud draft/input state is requested

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the Copilot extension's repository picker command
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One command invocation per explicit click; no collection fan-out
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Sandbox repository search was not available from the editor creation picker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the interactive repository-pick action waits for it

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Small fixed mode/approval schemas plus the deduplicated set of tracked repositories, at most one choice per workspace root.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cloud model catalog requests are coalesced globally; repository picker invocations are user-driven and not batched.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The model catalog caches a successful response until account change; failures are not automatically retried per draft and require retry. Repository choices reuse the root-resolution observable cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: load guards and account-generation invalidation are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog latency is service-dependent, but request count is bounded and coalesced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable regression: model network work is lazy and coalesced, and picker IPC is explicitly user initiated.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send the first prompt from a Cloud draft
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Repository inference must settle, then account lookup, remote sandbox creation, relay connection, session-type registration, optional host config confirmation, materialized session load/create, and first-turn dispatch occur in sequence. This is intentionally the provisioning critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve workspace repositories before inferring the clone target
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Uses the same one-per-unresolved-root cached Git opens; no repeat after choices settle
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The editor could not create a sandbox session before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: First send waits for all workspace choices when cold

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create one Mission Control sandbox task
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one per materialization attempt; same-draft concurrent sends coalesce in ChatService
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This boundary existed for Agents-window sandbox creation but was not reachable from editor draft send.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the draft can bind to a real environment

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Connect to the newly provisioned sandbox relay
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One connection attempt for the new unique environment; same-address connects coalesce
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing/discovered editor sessions connected on open; editor creation did not previously allocate and connect a new environment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before session provider/config/turn dispatch can proceed

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve and validate selected mode/approval configuration against the host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call when the draft carries recognized config picks; skipped for an empty config
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No editor sandbox draft config existed; Agents-window creation already performed equivalent confirmation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Intentionally blocks first send so a pick is not silently changed

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/subscribe the agent session if not already represented by host state, then dispatch the first turn
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One session create/subscription and one turn dispatch per successful first send; existing eager state avoids duplicate creation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This is the existing Agent Host session invocation path; the PR supplies initial config and model aliases without increasing per-turn boundary cardinality after materialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Final required stage before response progress

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One draft/session; repository wait scales with unresolved workspace roots, while provisioning/config/turn boundaries are constant per attempt.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ChatService coalesces concurrent materialization for the same untitled resource. Connects coalesce per address, but newly created environments have distinct addresses and there is no global provisioning limiter. The normal UI flow executes one materialization at a time per draft.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Repository results are cached per root; model catalog is account-cached; connection attempts are coalesced per address. Failed or canceled provisioning can be retried as a new remote task, with no cross-attempt task cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the boundary sequence and one-per-attempt cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cloud allocation and relay wake time vary. Repeated cancel/retry could create concurrent unique environments, but evidence is insufficient that normal UI usage creates a severe aggregate burst.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding beyond the eager startup work. The provisioning boundaries are intrinsic to the new feature, same-draft work is coalesced, and config confirmation is an intentional correctness gate.

Scenarios.Scenario: Discover, list, and resume existing sandbox sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Account-wide discovery seeds local providers without connecting. Opening a selected session then establishes its existing host connection and loads session state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List sandbox sessions from Mission Control
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced scan, with full/incremental retry policy independent of session count
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Needed to populate remote history, but not multiplied per listed session

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Connect to the selected sandbox environment on open
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced connection per environment address requested
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing sessions already connected on demand before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to resume a disconnected live session

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Discovered environments and sessions; remote listing is grouped in one discovery response, while connections occur only for environments opened.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Discovery is serialized/coalesced. Connections are coalesced per address rather than globally serialized.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Persisted inventory/history supports offline listing; discovery uses stale intervals and incremental progress, and connected/provisioning environments are retained during reconciliation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from discovery and connect ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Account history size varies, but the diff does not increase network calls per history item.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the refactor preserves grouped discovery and on-demand connection counts.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a sandbox from the Agents window after provisioning logic was moved shared
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Agents-window send still performs account lookup, one task creation, one connection, optional repository preparation/config confirmation, and one first-turn dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provision and connect one cloud sandbox
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same implementation and boundary ordering lived directly in the Agents-window subclass before being moved to the shared base.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One requested session; repository progress scans host project metadata locally as state updates arrive.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-address connection coalescing and discovery serialization are preserved by the move.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider seeding, inventory persistence, and connection ownership remain the same.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from deleted and added implementations matching the same flow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No meaningful magnitude uncertainty; this is predominantly code movement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression and no regression-fix record: the move preserves the prior performance mechanism rather than fixing a documented shipped regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Disable the sandbox feature while an empty Cloud draft is open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Availability change checks the current local model and clears an empty untitled draft whose type was withdrawn. No remote operation is awaited.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One visible chat widget/model per availability event.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Feature disable disposes draft models, providers, option groups, and cancels enabled-scope work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression; the added check is constant-time aside from existing local draft clearing and runs on infrequent availability changes.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 25 changed files. One medium-severity eager-work regression was submitted: an always-live draft-option observer now forces serialized extension-host Git repository opening for every unresolved workspace root after restoration, even without Cloud usage. Provisioning, model catalog, discovery, config, cleanup, and materialization paths were traced for boundary counts, caching, concurrency, and lifecycle; no other high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue or qualifying regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
